description:
Hi there! Thanks for stopping by! 👋

Are you actively looking for a new opportunity? Or just checking the market? Well… you might just be in the right place!

We are looking for a Senior Frontend Developer to join one of our squads where you will be supporting Lightspeed’s Hospitality product group on the mission to expand our reach into new markets and countries while enhancing our advanced hospitality commerce platform.
For this role specifically, you will be joining the team focused on enhancing our backoffice platform. Our mission is to empower our merchants with smooth onboarding and make it easy to configure and manage their business setup—no matter the size or complexity.

You will join a healthy and collaborative team, continuously improving our engineering practices, and delivering state-of-the-art technology, all while keeping it fun. Above all, your work will change the way the world experiences hospitality.

What you'll be responsible for:

  • Working alongside some of the most brilliant minds in the industry, you will contribute to the omnichannel product by building new features and creative workflows.

  • Design and create beautiful, elegant, and functional web applications.

  • Your daily tasks will be split between development of new features and supporting existing integrations with our partners, while new features will dominate as we constantly open new markets.

  • Report to the Team Lead of Development and have frequent interactions with Product Managers, Product Designers, and Platform Teams.

  • Take part in daily agile ceremonies, brainstorm on innovative ideas that challenge the status quo, and implement solutions.

  • Act as an advocate for the highest code quality and ownership while contributing to the health of the infrastructure.

  • Raise the bar and elevate your team by sharing knowledge and best practices while always seeking improvement and progress.

What you'll be bringing to the team:

  • Strong knowledge of JavaScript (ES6+), TypeScript and CSS-in-JS

  • Knowledge of React.js, Next.js, or similar technologies

  • Solid understanding of cross-browser/platform issues and solutions

  • Experience developing in a back-end for frontend layer

  • Familiarity with writing tests (e2e using Cypress) and ensuring the highest coding standards

  • Communication skills in English

  • Even better if you have, but not necessary:

  • Experience in the development of mobile-first applications

  • Familiarity with modern cloud infrastructures

  • A keen eye for UI/UX design

Who you are:

  • We look for problem solvers that do not shy away from tackling complexity and love critical thinkers

  • You have a strong will to learn, grow and get out of your comfort zone

  • You have great energy and passion for technology

What’s in it for you:

Come live the Lightspeed experience...

  • Ability to do your job in a truly flexible environment;

  • Genuine career opportunities in a company that’s creating new jobs every day;

  • Work in a team big enough for growth but lean enough to make a real impact.

 

… and enjoy a range of benefits that’ll keep you happy and healthy:

  • Lightspeed share scheme (we are all owners)

  • Flexible working policy and unlimited paid time off (yes, you read that right)

  • Mental health online platform and counselling & coaching services

  • ​​Health and wellness benefit

  • Volunteer day to be able to give back to society!

To all recruitment agencies: Lightspeed does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. If we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy, Lightspeed will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Where to from here?

Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here.

Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.

Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Our cloud commerce solution transforms and unifies online and physical operations, multichannel sales, expansion to new locations, global payments, financial solutions, and connection to supplier networks.

Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries.

title: Site Reliability Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
Deine Rolle

Du unterstützt uns dabei, die On-Premise-Cloud-Plattform von OVHcloud weiterzuentwickeln, zu betreiben und zu industrialisieren. Als Teil eines kleinen, erfahrenen Teams arbeitest du an unserer OpenStack-basierten Infrastruktur sowie am Kubernetes- und GitOps-Stack, auf dem unsere kundenorientierte Cloud-Plattform läuft. AI-Assisted Engineering ist dabei ein fester Bestandteil unserer täglichen Engineering-Praxis – von Spec-Driven Development über agentische Coding-Workflows bis hin zu Incident Response und Automatisierung. Die Plattform befindet sich aktiv im Aufbau, sodass du direkten Einfluss auf Architektur, Automatisierungsstrategie und den Einsatz von AI im Platform Engineering hast. Als Senior übernimmst du Ownership für deine Themen und gestaltest deinen fachlichen Schwerpunkt entlang deiner Stärken – mit Fokus auf Automation, Compute Lifecycle, Platform Engineering und AI Substrate.

Unser Tech Stack 🚀

· OpenStack · Kubernetes · KVM · Linux · Bare Metal · Ansible · Terraform · Go
· FluxCD / ArgoCD · Git· Python · Claude Code · Cursor · Agentic Coding Tooling

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du konzipierst und entwickelst unsere OpenStack-basierte On-Premise-Cloud-Infrastruktur mit dem Ziel, komplette Cloud-Umgebungen hochautomatisiert auf Bare Metal ausrollen und in Betrieb nehmen zu können.

  • Du entwickelst und betreibst Infrastructure as Code mit Ansible und Terraform sowie unsere Kubernetes- und GitOps-Workflows mit FluxCD / ArgoCD - unterstützt durch LLMs, agentische Workflows und automatisierte Test- und Review-Prozesse.

  • Du verantwortest den Lifecycle unserer Compute-Infrastruktur - von Bare Metal, Firmware und Provisionierung bis zu Hypervisoren und virtuellen Compute Nodes. Dazu gehören unter anderem Patching, Migrationen, Host Evacuations, Capacity Rebalancing und die Automatisierung eines stabilen Plattformbetriebs.

  • Du entwickelst unser AI Substrate und unsere Self-Healing-Strategie weiter - von strukturierten Knowledge Bases und agentischen Workflows für Incident Triage und Capacity Planning bis hin zur schrittweisen Automatisierung heutiger Runbooks.

  • Du konzipierst Tests für Non-Regression, Performance und Security, dokumentierst und paketierst Lösungen und verbesserst die Plattform kontinuierlich anhand von Telemetrie, Betriebserfahrungen und Nutzerfeedback.

title: Senior Product Engineer (DevTools & AI reliability, remote)
description:
(Fully remote, async-first, DevTools SaaS, 32-40h/week, time zones: UTC-3 to UTC+3)

The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken.

They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: end-to-end tests and synthetic monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.

Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel.

Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. You will build reliability for this kind of software.

Our stack is AI (Codex, Claude, use what you like best), Vue.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Golang, Postgres, ClickHouse and AWS. We ship to prod all day, every day. We practice Agile (not scrum) and take pride in good documentation and good looking products.

We’re a remote-first startup that keeps things simple—low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love building cool things, working async, actually listening to and working with customers, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!

What you'll do

Build and ship with AI

You will actively use coding agents for full stack development, from exploring solutions and generating scaffolding to refactoring, test generation and debugging. At Checkly we push the limits of AI tools every day.

Talk to our users

You will talk directly to the developers, DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams who are on-call, debugging incidents, or wiring Checkly into production pipelines. You will understand their workflows, pain points, and feedback. You use those conversations to validate ideas, course-correct early, and iterate on what you build. Customer calls and the weekly support rotation are part of the job, not a distraction from it.

Find the right problems to solve

In a world where the cost of building software trends to zero, the hard part is picking what to build. You will focus on real developer pain: flaky tests and flaky checks, unclear failures, noisy alerts. You will favour pragmatic solutions that ship quickly, validate assumptions in production, and compound into long-term reliability improvements.

Own your work end to end

From shaping the initial idea, through implementation and rollout, to watching how it behaves in production. You will take part in on-call and help support customers when things don’t work as expected.

What you should have

  • You have shipped features with AI, not just experimented with them. You have taken work from zero to shipped with a comparable stack, made implementation decisions that held up, and put things in front of real users.

  • You have built and run production software. You know the realities of operating software that people depend on: edge cases, incidents, regressions, and the need for observability and follow-up. You are not surprised when things break. You help fix them.

  • You can hold a product conversation, not just a technical one. You can look at a customer problem and reason about whether the thing we are about to build actually solves it.

  • You work well without an office around you. You are autonomous and self-motivated in a remote setup, and you still enjoy getting to know your colleagues and helping other people get unstuck.

  • FULLY remote role, within the UTC-3 to UTC+3 time zones. You need to be able to travel to (other) European countries without having to wait for a visa appointment, for our annual kickoff, a team meetup or a conference.

What you will hate about us

We would rather tell you now than have you find out in month two.

  • We use AI for everything, and we mean everything. AI skepticism is not a thing here. If you have the slightest hesitation about working with AI every day, this is not the place for you, and that is completely fine.

  • We write more than we talk. We are async-first, so a lot of decisions happen in documents and threads, not meetings. If you do your best thinking out loud in a room full of people, you will miss it here.

  • We are lean, so you own the unglamorous parts too. There is no separate QA team, no ops layer to hand things off to, and you are on the support rotation and the on-call rotation like everyone else.

  • We ship constantly and change our minds. Priorities move as we learn from customers. If you need long, stable planning cycles, this will feel chaotic.

  • Customer signals come first, and most of the time they matter more than your instinct. We build what customers actually want, not the clever thing we dreamed up.

Benefits

  • Transparent salary because your salary shouldn't be dictated by how good a negotiator you are. (more info below)

  • Remote-first, flexible work hours, async-first (low meeting, high productivity) and transparent culture

  • Become part of a fast-growing, international, and remote team where your work matters, and your impact won't get lost in layers of bureaucracy.

  • Stock options

  • 27 days of paid vacation + your local public holidays

  • Paid sick leave & up to 14 weeks of paid parental leave

  • Co-working budget or home office setup

  • Annual company kickoffs

  • Employee & contractor options

Find out more here.

What we pay

Fair, competitive, and transparent pay is very important for us. Therefore we work with a standardized salary calculator that includes several factors such as seniority level as well as location.

  • €88k - €105k for someone in a similar cost of market as UK, Germany etc, + stock options

  • €79k - €97k for someone in a similar cost of market as Spain, Poland, Ukraine etc, + stock options

Apply

Women, non-binary people and POC will seek to match a much higher percentage of requirements before applying. If you're not sure you're the right fit, apply anyway and let us know what you bring to the table. We'd love to hear from you!

The Role

We're looking for a QA Engineer to join our current QA team. You'll take ownership of how we test, validate, and sign off on quality across our platform. We're actively investing in our QA practice: expanding automated test coverage, improving our release testing process, and moving toward a model where quality is embedded throughout the development lifecycle.

You'll report to a technical Engineering Manager and work alongside engineers who value clear test documentation, reliable automation, and confident code releases.

As a mature company, we have legacy systems and established manual testing workflows, but we are transitioning to modern automated testing practices using Playwright and TypeScript. The split between manual and automated work varies, but you should be comfortable working across both, bringing automation where it adds the most value while pragmatically maintaining manual coverage where it's still the right tool.

A core goal of our QA evolution is to make testing faster, more reliable, and less dependent on last-minute changes before each release: replacing fragile manual regression cycles with stable automated suites, reducing flakiness, and building coverage that the whole team can rely on. Every testing investment is measured by whether it improves quality and reduces the team's burden at release time.

What You'll Do

  • Write and maintain automated regression tests; review automation MRs from peers

  • Execute manual testing across web UIs (functional, regression, cross-platform, responsive layouts on mobile/tablet)

  • Create and maintain test cases, checklists, and test documentation in TestRail

  • File clear, actionable bug reports with reproduction steps; collaborate with developers to triage and resolve

  • Own the release testing process to ensure only high-quality changes ship

  • Partner with PMs and designers on requirements review, edge cases, and acceptance criteria

  • Contribute to QA process improvements as we scale (currently a 2-person team growing to 4)

How We Work

We believe you should know what your days look like before you accept an offer.

We don't have much bureaucracy. Small team, direct communication, short decision loops. If you've worked at places where opening a Jira ticket to request a Jira ticket was normal, this isn't that. Here's the reality:

Meetings (yes, we keep them minimal):

  • Daily standup with your product team. Show up, share updates and unblock each other..

  • Sprint planning and retrospectives with your product team, once per sprint.

  • 1:1 with your Engineering Manager - Regular cadence, your agenda.

  • Monthly Engineering all-hands.

  • That's it. The rest of your time is yours to work.

Deployments:

  • Bi-monthly release cadence with a schedule published in advance. As a QA Engineer, you own the release testing window. Coordinating with developers, running regression suites, and signing off on quality before the release.

  • Infrequent ad-hoc hotfixes

Communication:

  • Async-friendly. Documentation-first.

  • Slack/ Jira/ GitLab MRs/ Notion

  • Google Workspace for email and documents.

  • Zoom for video calls.

Timezone:

  • We need significant overlap with typical CET (Central European Time) working hours to coordinate and collaborate synchronously. Additionally we have stakeholders and developers in US timezones that we occasionally need to meet.


What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years of QA engineering experience, including web UI testing

  • 2+ years of experience with Playwright or a similar test automation framework (e.g. Cypress, Selenium, Puppeteer)

  • 2+ years of experience using TypeScript

  • Strong test design skills: comfortable writing and maintaining test cases, checklists, and test documentation

  • Familiarity with QA's role in the SDLC and how to collaborate with developers and PMs

  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail

  • Upper-intermediate English (B2+) for written and spoken communication

  • Strong experience in manual testing and writing manual test cases

Nice to have:

How you’ll work with other teams:

Career Growth

We have a defined career ladder. Whether your path leads toward Senior/Staff QA Engineer or Engineering Management, there's room to grow - and we'll work with you to get there.

Onboarding

Every team member gets full support throughout onboarding, and no one expects you to figure out the ins and outs on your own. We'll pair with you, answer every question, and make sure you have the context you need. New hires typically feel very supported at Miaplaza.

What success looks like here: In the first couple of months, you're asking a lot of clarifying questions, reading documentation, exploring the product independently, and writing and running tests with confidence. By months 3-4, you're taking ownership of a specific area, building out test coverage, identifying gaps, and driving quality improvements. By month 5-6, you're contributing meaningfully to the testing strategy for migration and modernisation work and operating independently. The common thread: curiosity, initiative, and the habit of investigating before you ask, but always asking when you need to.

Interview Process

Our process is staged and designed to respect your time. Expect a mix of introductory conversation, technical discussion, and practical evaluation. We want to understand how you think about real problems and testing practices. As part of the process, we will ask for professional references and conduct a background check in accordance with applicable law. If you need any accommodations during the interview process, let us know, we're happy to help.
